title: The Automated Excuse Generator
subtitle: How a late arrival becomes a plausible story.

nodes.label: Spot the Delay
nodes.summary: Notice you are late and see who is waiting.
nodes.description: The tool notices that you are running behind and works out who is expecting you and how many minutes late you will be by the time you finally arrive.

nodes.label: Gather the Facts
nodes.summary: Collect the traffic, weather, and calendar details.
nodes.description: This step pulls together the small true details that make a story believable, such as the weather outside, the state of the roads, and what your calendar claims you were doing.

nodes.label: Write the Excuse
nodes.summary: A model turns the facts and tone into one short line.
nodes.description: A single model reads the facts and the chosen tone, then writes one short note that sounds sorry, stays vague enough to survive questions, and quietly blames something other than you.
nodes.modelSelection: Uses a small, fast model, because a late note does not deserve your very best thinking.

prompts.label: Excuse prompt
prompts.summary: This prompt asks for a short, sincere reason you are late that nobody can disprove.

nodes.label: Believable Enough?
nodes.summary: Judge whether the excuse would actually hold up.
nodes.description: Here the tool reads the draft the way a suspicious friend would and decides whether the story is convincing enough to deliver or too flimsy to risk, throwing weak drafts back for another try.

nodes.label: Send It
nodes.summary: Fire off the winning excuse and brace yourself.
nodes.description: Once a draft passes the check, the tool delivers your chosen excuse to whoever is waiting, marks the moment you committed to the story, and then leaves you alone to live with it.

nodes.label: The Sent Note
nodes.summary: The finished note the tool ends up sending.
nodes.description: This is the exact wording the tool settled on, kept nearby so that you can reread it later and remember which convenient story you committed to on this particular morning.

edges.label: running late
edges.summary: Realizing you are late starts the whole rescue effort.

edges.label: facts + tone
edges.summary: The collected details and the chosen tone feed the writer.

edges.label: draft
edges.summary: The freshly written draft goes to the believability gate.

edges.label: believable
edges.summary: A convincing draft is cleared for sending.

edges.label: too flimsy
edges.summary: A weak draft is thrown back for another attempt.

edges.label: saved copy
edges.summary: Each finished note is kept so you can see the exact wording.
